connection: Session 24 added tested production exceptions. Session 25 now uses a deliberately constructed ScratchPad experiment because the production total-hours path filters out open entries before calling GetDuartion.
objectives: Trace how an exception travels upward until matching code catches it, and explain why an unhandled console exception terminates the process.
Explain that IDisposable defines a cleanup contract and requires a public Dispose method.
Use a using block to guarantee Dispose runs when control leaves its protected scope, including when an exception leaves the block.
Use the memory anchor: Leave the using scope; run Dispose.

visuals.title: An exception travels upward until matching code catches it
visuals.explanation: In this deliberately constructed ScratchPad experiment, InvalidOperationException leaves the using block and continues to the matching catch outside it. This is not presented as an existing production App path.

visuals.title: No matching catch means the console process terminates
visuals.explanation: If an exception reaches the top of a console program without being handled, the runtime reports it and terminates the process. The experiment catches its deliberate failure so ScratchPad can continue.

visuals.title: Leave the using scope; run Dispose
visuals.explanation: Normal completion and an exception are two ways to leave the protected using scope. Either way, Dispose runs before control continues beyond that scope.

visuals.title: IDisposable defines a cleanup contract
visuals.explanation: The private DisposalProbe simulates cleanup. Real disposable resources can include streams, database connections, contexts, and other external handles; ordinary classes should not implement IDisposable without cleanup to perform.

preQuiz.prompt: If a called method throws and the current method has no matching catch, what happens next?
options: The exception travels upward to the caller
The method silently returns a default value
Dispose converts it into a warning
preQuiz.explanation: An exception continues upward until matching code catches it or it reaches the top of the process.

preQuiz.prompt: When does a using block dispose its resource?
options: When execution leaves the using block, including by exception
preQuiz.explanation: Leave the using scope; run Dispose.

preQuiz.prompt: Why must DisposalProbe.Dispose be public even though DisposalProbe is private?
options: Dispose fulfills the public IDisposable interface contract
Every method in a private class must be public
using cannot call methods on private classes
preQuiz.explanation: An interface implementation must provide the interface's publicly callable member.

concept.title: Production audit: do not invent a reachable failure
paragraphs: The cumulative repository spells the method GetDuartion, and its real signature returns non-nullable TimeSpan. ClockEntry.ClockOut is DateTime?, ClockEntryService uses Clockout, and the open-entry message is Employee has not clcoked out yet.

Program.cs in the cumulative repository calls PayrollService.CalculateTotalHours, but ClockEntryRepository.GetEmployeeClockEntries filters for ClockOut != null before CalculateTotalHours sums GetDuartion(). That means an open entry does not travel through this production path. Session 25 therefore does not add a meaningless App try/catch or change production behavior to manufacture a failure.

concept.title: A focused experiment makes propagation observable
paragraphs: ResourceExperiments deliberately throws InvalidOperationException inside using. The using body does not catch it, so control leaves the using scope, Dispose runs, and the same exception continues to the matching catch outside using.

The experiment catches the failure so ScratchPad can print the probe's final state. Without that matching catch, the exception would continue to the top-level console statements and terminate the process.

concept.title: IDisposable and the nested helper
paragraphs: IDisposable defines one cleanup member: public void Dispose(). Dispose is public because it fulfills the public interface contract, even though DisposalProbe itself is private. The probe simulates cleanup; IDisposable is for types that genuinely need deterministic cleanup, not every ordinary class.

A nested class is declared inside another class. DisposalProbe belongs inside ResourceExperiments but outside Run. private means only the containing ResourceExperiments class can use it, and ResourceExperiments can construct it normally. Nesting is useful here because the helper belongs only to this experiment; IDisposable does not require nesting, and a separate class could implement it.
Memory anchor: Outer class runs the experiment. Nested class supports it.

concept.title: The property records proof of cleanup
paragraphs: public bool WasDisposed { get; private set; } is an auto-implemented property, so C# supplies its backing field. Other code can read it, only DisposalProbe can change it, and bool begins as false by default.

Dispose changes the property after construction, so the property needs private set. A get-only auto-property could not be assigned later inside Dispose. Memory anchor: Others may read it; only the object may change it.
concept.code: public bool WasDisposed { get; private set; }

concept.title: Using block, using declaration, and variable scope
paragraphs: A using block disposes when execution leaves that block: using (probe) { /* protected scope */ }. A using declaration such as using DisposalProbe probe = new(); disposes when execution leaves the containing scope.

A variable declared inside try cannot be referenced after catch. This experiment declares probe before try so it remains in scope for the final check, uses it inside a using block to guarantee cleanup, and catches the deliberate exception so execution can continue.
Memory anchor: Declare outside to observe afterward. Use inside to guarantee cleanup.

lab.title: Prove Cleanup During Exception Propagation
lab.objective: Build a focused ScratchPad experiment proving that Dispose runs before an exception reaches a matching catch outside a using block.
lab.task: Create ResourceExperiments and a private nested DisposalProbe, deliberately throw inside using, catch outside it, then print proof that cleanup already ran.
lab.startingCondition: The ScratchPad project exists at src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.ScratchPad and Program.cs preserves all earlier experiment calls. Production App code remains unchanged.

steps.text: In project src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.ScratchPad, create folder Session25 and file src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.ScratchPad/Session25/ResourceExperiments.cs. Setup code: paste a starter comment identifying this as the deliberately constructed Session 25 cleanup experiment.

In project src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.ScratchPad, folder Session25, file ResourceExperiments.cs, declare public sealed class ResourceExperiments. Inside the ResourceExperiments class body, declare public void Run() with an empty body. Learning code: write the class and method yourself.

In project src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.ScratchPad, folder Session25, file ResourceExperiments.cs, inside ResourceExperiments but outside ResourceExperiments.Run, declare private sealed class DisposalProbe : IDisposable. A nested class is a class inside another class: ResourceExperiments runs the experiment and its private nested class supports it. IDisposable does not require nesting. Learning code: write the declaration yourself.

In project src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.ScratchPad, folder Session25, file ResourceExperiments.cs, inside ResourceExperiments.DisposalProbe, stub public void Dispose() with an empty body. Dispose must be public because it implements the public IDisposable contract, even though DisposalProbe is private. Build the ScratchPad project to keep errors local.

In project src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.ScratchPad, folder Session25, file ResourceExperiments.cs, inside the ResourceExperiments.DisposalProbe class body, add public bool WasDisposed { get; private set; }. This auto-implemented property starts false; other code may read it, but only DisposalProbe may change it. private set lets Dispose assign it later; a get-only auto-property would not. Learning code: write the property yourself.

In project src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.ScratchPad, folder Session25, file ResourceExperiments.cs, inside ResourceExperiments.DisposalProbe.Dispose, set WasDisposed to true, then print exactly DisposalProbe cleanup ran. Learning code: write both statements yourself.

In project src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.ScratchPad, folder Session25, file ResourceExperiments.cs, as the first statement inside ResourceExperiments.Run, before any try block, construct DisposalProbe and store it in a local variable named probe. It must be declared before try so ResourceExperiments.Run can read probe after catch.

In project src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.ScratchPad, folder Session25, file ResourceExperiments.cs, inside ResourceExperiments.Run immediately after creating probe, add try and catch (InvalidOperationException exception) blocks. Keep using inside try and catch outside using so the experiment can observe propagation and continue.

In project src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.ScratchPad, folder Session25, file ResourceExperiments.cs, inside the try block in ResourceExperiments.Run, add a using (probe) block. This is a using block: it disposes when control leaves that block. A using declaration disposes at the end of its containing scope; declaring that variable inside try would also make it unavailable after catch.

In project src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.ScratchPad, folder Session25, file ResourceExperiments.cs, inside the using (probe) block in ResourceExperiments.Run, deliberately throw new InvalidOperationException with the exact message Intentional Session 25 failure. Learning code: write the throw yourself.

In project src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.ScratchPad, folder Session25, file ResourceExperiments.cs, inside the catch block in ResourceExperiments.Run, print exception.Message. Then, after catch but still inside ResourceExperiments.Run, print probe.WasDisposed using the exact label Was disposed:. This proves Dispose ran before catch handled the exception.

In project src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.ScratchPad, file src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.ScratchPad/Program.cs, inside the top-level program after all earlier experiment calls, construct ResourceExperiments in a variable named session25 and call session25.Run(). Do not remove earlier calls.

From the csharp-learn-with-ai solution folder, run project src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.ScratchPad and verify ResourceExperiments.Run prints this exact order: cleanup message, intentional failure message, then Was disposed: True. Next build PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln and run its full test suite. Open Solution Reveal only after your output and checks agree.

reveals.title: Solution
reveals.text: The using body throws; leaving using runs Dispose; the exception continues to catch; catch handles it; execution continues and prints the recorded state.

lab.expectedBehavior:
DisposalProbe cleanup ran.
Intentional Session 25 failure.
Was disposed: True

Execution order: (1) using body throws, (2) execution leaves using, (3) Dispose runs, (4) the exception continues to catch, (5) catch handles it, and (6) execution continues after catch.

postQuiz.explanation: Leave the using scope; run Dispose. The exception reaches catch only after cleanup.

Because IDisposable variables must be fields
postQuiz.explanation: A variable declared inside try cannot be referenced after catch.

reflections: Why must Dispose run before the matching catch handles the exception?
Why does the experiment declare probe before try but place using inside try?
When would a separate disposable class be clearer than a private nested helper?
whatBreaks: Removing using means the experiment no longer guarantees cleanup when the throw skips later statements. Moving probe inside try makes it unavailable after catch, so the final proof cannot compile. Removing catch lets the deliberate exception reach ScratchPad's top-level statements and terminate the console process.
summary: Session 25 uses a deliberately constructed ScratchPad experiment rather than claiming a reachable production failure. The using body throws, leaving using runs Dispose, the exception continues to the matching catch, and execution then prints WasDisposed as proof. Leave the using scope; run Dispose.
